title: Health Informatics Specialists
description: Apply knowledge of nursing and informatics to assist in the design, development, and ongoing modification of computerized health care systems. May educate staff and assist in problem solving to promote the implementation of the health care system.

tasks.text: Use informatics science to design or implement health information technology applications for resolution of clinical or health care administrative problems.

Apply knowledge of computer science, information science, nursing, and informatics theory to nursing practice, education, administration, or research, in collaboration with other health informatics specialists.

Inform local, state, national, and international health policies related to information management and communication, confidentiality and security, patient safety, infrastructure development, and economics.
Analyze and interpret patient, nursing, or information systems data to improve nursing services.
Identify, collect, record, or analyze data relevant to the nursing care of patients.

clusters.label: Judging the Qualities of Objects, Services, or People

tasks.text: Develop, implement, or evaluate health information technology applications, tools, processes, or structures to assist nurses with data management.
Analyze computer and information technologies to determine applicability to nursing practice, education, administration, and research.
Develop or implement policies or practices to ensure the privacy, confidentiality, or security of patient information.
Plan, install, repair, or troubleshoot telehealth technology applications or systems in homes.

clusters.label: Communicating with Supervisors, Peers, or Subordinates

tasks.text: Translate nursing practice information between nurses and systems engineers, analysts, or designers, using object-oriented models or other techniques.

Design, develop, select, test, implement, and evaluate new or modified informatics solutions, data structures, and decision-support mechanisms to support patients, health care professionals, and their information management and human-computer and human-technology interactions within health care contexts.

clusters.label: Communicating with People Outside the Organization

tasks.text: Disseminate information about nursing informatics science and practice to the profession, other health care professions, nursing students, and the public.
Develop strategies, policies or procedures for introducing, evaluating, or modifying information technology applied to nursing practice, administration, education, or research.
Read current literature, talk with colleagues, and participate in professional organizations or conferences to keep abreast of developments in informatics.
Develop or deliver training programs for health information technology, creating operating manuals as needed.
Design, conduct, or provide support to nursing informatics research.
Provide consultation to nurses regarding hardware or software configuration.

skills.name: Reading Comprehension
skills.def: Understanding written sentences and paragraphs in work-related documents.

skills.name: Complex Problem Solving
skills.def: Identifying complex problems and reviewing related information to develop and evaluate options and implement solutions.

skills.name: Active Listening
skills.def: Giving full attention to what other people are saying, taking time to understand the points being made, asking questions as appropriate, and not interrupting at inappropriate times.

skills.name: Writing
skills.def: Communicating effectively in writing as appropriate for the needs of the audience.

skills.name: Speaking
skills.def: Talking to others to convey information effectively.

skills.name: Critical Thinking
skills.def: Using logic and reasoning to identify the strengths and weaknesses of alternative solutions, conclusions, or approaches to problems.

skills.name: Judgment and Decision Making
skills.def: Considering the relative costs and benefits of potential actions to choose the most appropriate one.

skills.name: Active Learning
skills.def: Understanding the implications of new information for both current and future problem-solving and decision-making.

skills.name: Learning Strategies
skills.def: Selecting and using training/instructional methods and procedures appropriate for the situation when learning or teaching new things.

skills.name: Systems Analysis
skills.def: Determining how a system should work and how changes in conditions, operations, and the environment will affect outcomes.

skills.name: Systems Evaluation
skills.def: Identifying measures or indicators of system performance and the actions needed to improve or correct performance, relative to the goals of the system.

skills.name: Monitoring
skills.def: Monitoring/Assessing performance of yourself, other individuals, or organizations to make improvements or take corrective action.

skills.name: Coordination
skills.def: Adjusting actions in relation to others' actions.

skills.name: Instructing
skills.def: Teaching others how to do something.

skills.name: Time Management
skills.def: Managing one's own time and the time of others.

skills.name: Social Perceptiveness
skills.def: Being aware of others' reactions and understanding why they react as they do.

skills.name: Service Orientation
skills.def: Actively looking for ways to help people.

skills.name: Management of Personnel Resources
skills.def: Motivating, developing, and directing people as they work, identifying the best people for the job.

skills.name: Mathematics
skills.def: Using mathematics to solve problems.

skills.name: Persuasion
skills.def: Persuading others to change their minds or behavior.

skills.name: Object or component oriented development software
skills.def: Software to create or maintain applications using object-oriented programming concepts. Examples: Computer aided software engineering CASE tools, Microsoft SQL Server Reporting Services SSRS, Perl, Python.

skills.name: Business intelligence and data analysis software
skills.def: Software to present, visualize, or analyze data to help businesses make informed decisions. Examples: Microsoft Power BI, Qlik software, Qlik Tech QlikView, Tableau.

skills.name: Analytical or scientific software
skills.def: Software to capture data, perform analysis, or generate reports or visualizations to support scientific research. Examples: IBM SPSS Statistics, SAS.

skills.name: Data base user interface and query software
skills.def: Software to query, present, or edit information stored in a database sytem. Examples: Microsoft Access, Structured query language SQL.

skills.name: Spreadsheet software
skills.def: Software to create or edit numbers or text organized into rows and columns of cells. May include formulas which recalculate values based on other cells. Examples: Microsoft Excel.

skills.name: Office suite software
skills.def: Software to provide word processing, spreadsheet, e-mail, presentations, or data management capabilities. Examples: Microsoft Office software.
